profiles.label: TCL (Google TV)
steps: On the TV open Settings → System → About.
Scroll to "Android TV OS build" and press OK on the remote 7 times until it says you are a developer.
Go back to Settings → System → Developer options and turn on "USB debugging".
Find the TV's IP address: Settings → Network & Internet → your Wi-Fi network → IP address.
Click Connect here. The TV shows "Allow USB debugging?" — tick "Always allow from this computer" and choose Allow.
profiles.notes: TCL Google TV sets accept network ADB on port 5555 once USB debugging is on. If Connect keeps failing, turn USB debugging off and on again, or restart the TV.

profiles.label: TCL (older Android TV)
steps: On the TV open Settings → Device Preferences → About.
Select "Build" and press OK 7 times.
Go back to Device Preferences → Developer options and turn on "USB debugging".
Find the IP: Settings → Network & Internet → your Wi-Fi → IP address.
Click Connect and accept the "Allow USB debugging?" prompt on the TV.

profiles.label: Other Android TV / Google TV
steps: Open Settings and find About (under System or Device Preferences).
Press OK on "Build" or "Android TV OS build" 7 times to unlock Developer options.
In Developer options turn on "USB debugging" (or "Network debugging").
Find the TV's IP address under Network & Internet.
Click Connect and accept the prompt on the TV. If your TV only offers "Wireless debugging" with a pairing code, use the Pair option instead.
